builds.howItPlays: You answer each unit your opponent plays with cheap removal and bounce spells, and once you've targeted their units or gear twice in a turn, Ezreal draws you a card. Pack of Wonders, a 2-cost gear, returns your own Treasure Trove or Bewitching Spirit to your hand so you can replay it for another card or another discard from your opponent, and late in the game Thousand-Tailed Watcher, a 7-cost unit that shrinks every enemy unit as it arrives, takes over the battlefields.
builds.whyYou: You like having an answer for everything and don't mind letting your opponent make the first move. You enjoy a long game where every removal spell trades one for one and small edges pile up: an extra card from Ezreal, a Treasure Trove played a second time, until they have nothing left to play. You'll put very few units down in the early turns and score your points late. If patience and a full hand of answers sound more fun than racing to the finish, this Ezreal suits you.

Convergence #3 Top 16 | 1st - berkun (Axikyo; the result claim is unverified) https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/72d44405-bb49-400e-8a2a-0a5f90321c6f Control 3/3/7.5/2.5. Adjustments on every sheet: complexity +1, because the Legend's draw needs two enemy targets in a turn, so spells are sequenced around it every turn; variance -1, because the Legend draws a card most turns. Cards that decided each Axis. Pace: no units costing 2 or less, and 3 to 4 cards costing 5+ (Thousand-Tailed Watcher, Singularity, Mindsplitter). Stance: 24 to 26 answers (Gust, Wages of Pain, Deadly Flourish, Bellows Breath, Star-Crossed, The List, Vex, Bewitching Spirit) against one pressure card (Sprite Fountain), balance -0.57 to -0.63. Complexity: 11 to 13 reactive cards (Gust, Stupefy, Star-Crossed, Wages of Pain, Hard Bargain), 12 setup/modes cards (Pack of Wonders, The List, Fizz, Bellows Breath), plus the Legend adjustment. Variance: 17 to 19 removal spells, no luck or swing cards, 60 to 75% of the list as 3-ofs. No Axis gap between formula and judgment reached 2; the largest was stance, 3.8 formula against 2.5 judged. Legend ability: exhaust Ezreal as a Reaction to draw 1, usable only once you've chosen enemy units and/or gear twice that turn with spells or unit abilities. Also played: Temporal Breach Bounce (replays entry-effect units through blink spells) https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/d8b24e31-0d82-40ed-ac02-f5c18d777719 Midrange 5/4.5/8/5; Treasure Hunter Tempo (cheap movers and reaction-speed bounce, no gear engine) https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/8dd4c2db-5cd7-49f4-8369-66a8373ff024 Tempo 5/4/7.5/3 and https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/a94dac22-e6d4-4fe2-9c5e-7cca6bddaa95 Tempo 5.5/5/7.5/3; Plundering Poro (cheap units that grow off spells or make Gold) https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/af9dbc10-f29e-47ee-b923-3ed35925cea7 Midrange 5/4.5/7/3, https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/0e5ddfc0-350f-4c3b-994f-75cc013b2922 Control 4.5/4/7/2.5 and https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/120dbd88-5635-43d5-a809-752d4ba94cf1 Midrange 5.5/5/7/3. Each of these is a lone list or thin evidence, so none clears the Played bar alone. Confidence: high. For the reviewer: the Applied Researchers spell style (Zuno D Viko, Filosseno) is left out as dead because every list runs the banned Stacked Deck, and it was not merged into Poro. If a legal version appears, reconsider merging it with the Poro style into a second, faster Build.
